main_body: A brown gnarled tree-trunk or root mass with a few dark green moss patches, set on grey stone tiles. It is a small organic object about 16x16 px.
top_band: none. The column reads as brown trunk or root bark with no distinct lighter horizontal top surface. At the top it is dark brown and green moss against grey stone.
evidence: Reading a central column from row 0 down, there is dark brown bark with a green moss patch and then brown trunk texture continuing to the base. No lighter horizontal band, front-edge line or eave shadow is present. The object is drawn as a flat front view of a trunk or root mass, with no top surface visible. Strictly this fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The reference trees have rich leaf canopies in 5 or more greens and a shaded trunk with roots. The candidate is a small brown trunk fragment in about 3 browns with a few dark green moss dots. It has no canopy, little shading depth and visibly less tile density than the references. The outline is a dark brown tone, which is acceptable, but the piece is much thinner than the references.
